algorithm.Title: Head Lice - Male (Adult)
algorithm.ContentSet: IST Open-Source Guideline Content | Adult | Male
Definition: Qatar-localized UAT-only adult and pediatric pathway for suspected head lice, requiring confirmation, age/pregnancy review, safe product selection and safeguarding assessment.
algorithm.Author: IST Health Open-Source Guideline Content
algorithm.LastRevised: RESEARCH_REQUIRED - internal IST clinical adaptation date is not recorded
algorithm.Copyright: Public-source content reused under its stated licence. This is not licensed STCC content.

questions.Question: Have no live lice been found, and is a widespread rash or redness the main concern?
questions.Information: A widespread rash without confirmed live lice belongs in the Rash or Redness - Widespread pathway.

questions.Question: Have medicated treatments already been tried without success?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance recommends speaking to a pharmacist about alternative treatments if the first attempt hasn't worked.

questions.Question: Is this a new case of suspected or confirmed head lice with none of the features above?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance states head lice can be treated without primary-care review, using wet combing or pharmacy treatments.

advice.Title: Head lice treatment not working
Content: Ask a pharmacist about alternative treatment options.
Call Back If: lice persist after a second treatment.

advice.Title: Confirmed head-lice management review
Content: Confirm live lice with appropriate combing and obtain pharmacist/clinician advice before selecting treatment for age, pregnancy, breastfeeding, allergies and prior exposure. Do not use pesticides, veterinary products, essential oils, heat or flammable remedies.
Call Back If: scalp infection or chemical injury; lice persist despite correctly supervised treatment.

references: NHS.UK, "Head lice", https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/head-lice/ (page last reviewed 22 April 2024)
searchwords: lice crawling in my kids hair
